newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebel governor appointed for Zaire's Shaba region.
newsitem.headline: Rebel governor appointed for Zaire's Shaba region.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila appointed a provisional governor for mineral-rich Shaba province on Monday and delayed elections to let the confused situation settle, the new governor said.
Gaetan Kakudji told a news conference in Lubumbashi he would act as interim governor in the name of Kabila's Alliance of Democtatic Forces for Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) rebels.
Analysts said Kabila's alliance could face its biggest political challenge yet in Shaba province, with its history of ethnic tension and separatist sentiment.

The appointment of Kakudji effectively stalled an attempt by the incumbent Shaba governor to ride on Kabila's coat-tails back into office under the new government -- a move many opponents of Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko said would have been tantamount to stealing the revolution.

An alliance spokesman, asked to explain the reasons for delaying elections in Shaba, told a news conference there was confusion and the alliance felt it was "not appropriate to go into detail on what's going on".

Kakudji said the alliance was committed to establishing a "social market economy" that would attract foreign investors, but would let the people of Shaba benefit from the wealth that Mobutu's regime had plundered from them for the past 30 years.
